happened: In August 2025, President Trump directed the Commerce Department to start work on a new census that would leave out immigrants in the U.S. illegally. In February 2026, the Census Bureau proposed using a form with a citizenship question (taken from the American Community Survey) in its 2026 test for the 2030 census, planned for two sites from April to September 2026. Whether the question would be approved for the test or the 2030 census was not decided.

key_dates.event: President directs Commerce to begin work on a new census excluding people in the U.S. illegally.
Census Bureau proposes a citizenship question in its 2026 field test.

legal: No court ruling on the test was found. Several Republican-led states have sued to exclude people without legal status from census counts; New York officials said in April 2026 they would consider legal action if the question is previewed for 2030.
closeness: Same idea, but only a test so far. The list of 2030 census topics is due to Congress in 2027, and the Supreme Court blocked a similar question for the 2020 census.
uncertain: Whether OMB approved the citizenship question for the test, and whether the test ran as planned, were not confirmed. Newest source: April 2026.

happened: On September 10, 2026, the Census Bureau proposed a rule that would bar any question about race, ethnicity or sexual orientation from the decennial census form used to count people. The comment period was extended to November 2, 2026. This would replace the planned combined race and ethnicity question from the 2024 federal standards with no such question at all on that form.

key_dates.event: Census Bureau proposes barring race and ethnicity questions from the census form.
Extended comment deadline.

closeness: The administration did take control of the question, but went further than review: the proposal would drop race and ethnicity from the census count form, while keeping them on the American Community Survey.
uncertain: Whether OMB has changed its 2024 race and ethnicity standards, and whether a final rule will be issued or challenged. Newest source is October 2026.
